Algebra I · Lesson 6.1

Ratios, Simple and Subtle

Solve this lesson →All lessons

Chapter 5 removed letters from a system one at a time. Chapter 6 opens by putting one in. Prealgebra chapter 7 settled what a:ba:b says. What is new here is algebraic. Naming the size of one part with a letter turns a ratio statement into an equation, and chapters 4 and 5 already solve equations. Start with a ratio and a total.

Problem
A bindery finishes 552 booklets, stapled to sewn in the ratio 7:57:5. Doubling both parts of 7:57:5 gives 14:1014:10, which totals 2424, and tripling gives 21:1521:15, which totals 3636. Keep scaling both parts by the same number until the two counts total 552552, then enter the number of stapled booklets.
Show a hint
  • The scaled totals 2424 and 3636 are both multiples of 1212, and 1212 is 7+57+5. Scaling both parts by the same number multiplies the total by that number as well.
  • 552÷12=46552÷12=46, so both parts of 7:57:5 get multiplied by 4646.
Show the full solution
Since 7+5=127+5=12 and 552÷12=46552÷12=46, both parts get multiplied by 4646, and the stapled count is 7(46)=3227(46)=322​. The sewn count is 5(46)=2305(46)=230, and 322+230=552322+230=552. Every scaled total is a multiple of 1212, so dividing 552552 by 1212 gives the multiplier in one step instead of testing 22, 33, 44 and on up.
Problem
A stadium has 493 seats, covered seats to open seats in the ratio 9:89:8. Write the two counts as 9k9k and 8k8k for a single number kk, form one equation from the total, and enter the number of covered seats.
Show a hint
  • Let kk be the size of one part, so the covered seats number 9k9k, the open seats number 8k8k, and the two counts together make 493493.
  • 9k+8k9k+8k collects to 17k17k, so the equation reads 17k=49317k=493, a one-letter equation of the kind 4.2 solves.
Show the full solution
9k+8k=4939k+8k=493 collects to 17k=49317k=493, so k=29k=29 and the covered seats number 9(29)=2619(29)=261​. The open seats number 8(29)=2328(29)=232, and 261+232=493261+232=493. Naming the part size kk makes the whole problem the single division 493÷17493÷17.
Key idea
The common multiplier. A ratio a:ba:b says the two amounts are akak and bkbk for one number kk, the size of one part. Multiplying both parts by the same number leaves the comparison unchanged, and every pair with that comparison is akak and bkbk for some kk, so nothing is lost by writing them that way. With a stated total the counts add to (a+b)k(a+b)k, and with three parts to (a+b+c)k(a+b+c)k, so that sum equals the total, one letter and one equation, which chapter 4 finishes in a single division. Scaling by hand finds the same kk one step at a time.
Problem
A workshop owns 378 hand tools, all of them hammers or chisels, with hammers to chisels in the ratio 5:95:9. A student computes 5995​ of 378378 and reports 210210 hammers. Enter the correct number of hammers.
Show a hint
  • The ratio 5:95:9 compares hammers with chisels, while 378378 is the total of both kinds. A fraction of that total is taken over both kinds together, not over the chisels alone.
  • The tools split into 5+9=145+9=14 equal parts, and the hammers are 55 of those parts.
Show the full solution
The tools split into 5+9=145+9=14 equal parts, so one part is 378÷14=27378÷14=27 tools and the number of hammers is 5(27)=1355(27)=135​. There are 9(27)=2439(27)=243 chisels, and 135+243=378135+243=378. Hammers are 514145​ of the tools, not 5995​, and with 210210 hammers only 168168 chisels remain, more hammers than chisels, the reverse of 5:95:9.
Problem
A nursery grows 984 saplings, oak, maple and pine, in the ratio 6:7:116:7:11. Write the three counts as 6k6k, 7k7k and 11k11k, and enter the number of pine saplings.
Show a hint
  • All three counts are built from the same kk, so they add to 6k+7k+11k6k+7k+11k, and that sum is 984984.
  • 6k+7k+11k6k+7k+11k collects to 24k24k, so 24k=98424k=984.
Show the full solution
6k+7k+11k=9846k+7k+11k=984 collects to 24k=98424k=984, so k=41k=41 and the pine count is 11(41)=45111(41)=451​. The others are 6(41)=2466(41)=246 oak and 7(41)=2877(41)=287 maple, and 246+287+451=984246+287+451=984. With three parts the sum has one more term than with two, and the rest of the method is the same.
Key idea
Part to part against part to whole. A ratio a:ba:b compares the two parts with each other. The first part's share of the whole is aa+ba+ba​, since the amounts are akak and bkbk, the whole is (a+b)k(a+b)k, and cancelling kk from ak(a+b)k(a+b)kak​ leaves aa+ba+ba​. With three parts it is aa+b+ca+b+ca​. Since a+ba+b is larger than bb, abba​ is larger than aa+ba+ba​, so reading a part-to-part ratio as a share of the whole overstates that part. The 5:95:9 hammers are 514145​ of the tools and 5995​ of the chisels.

Writing x:y=a:bx:y=a:b is writing xy=abyx​=ba​, and that is an equation in two letters. Multiply both sides by yy and then by bb, which is 4.4's move done twice, and what is left is bx=aybx=ay. Each numerator is multiplied whole, parentheses and all. Neither side is a fraction any more, so bx=aybx=ay is linear in xx and yy.

Problem
The crates and pallets in a depot are in the ratio 12:712:7, and the depot has 224 pallets. Let cc be the number of crates, so that statement is the equation c224=127224c​=712​. Cross-multiply, solve, and enter the number of crates.
Show a hint
  • Both sides are single fractions, so clear the denominators. Multiply both sides by 224224 and then by 77, and see what is left.
  • Clearing gives 7c=224×127c=224×12. Since 224=7×32224=7×32, divide by 77 before multiplying by 1212, which keeps the numbers small.
Show the full solution
Cross-multiplying c224=127224c​=712​ gives 7c=26887c=2688, so c=384c=384​. Check, 384224224384​ reduces to 127712​. In the ratio, crates come first, so 1212 is the numerator on the same side as cc. With the 1212 and 77 swapped the result would be 224×71212224×7​, not a whole number of crates.
Problem
The ratio of 5(x−4)+3x5(x−4)+3x to 2(x+21)2(x+21) is 3:13:1. Collect like terms on each side first, then cross-multiply and enter the value of xx.
Show a hint
  • A ratio of 3:13:1 says the first quantity is 33 times the second. Distribute the 2.1 way and combine like terms the 2.4 way on each side, then write that sentence as an equation.
  • The sides collect to 8x−208x−20 and 2x+422x+42, so the statement reads 8x−20=3(2x+42)8x−20=3(2x+42).
Show the full solution
Distributing gives 5x−20+3x=8x−205x−20+3x=8x−20 on the left and 2x+422x+42 on the right, so 8x−202x+42=312x+428x−20​=13​, and cross-multiplying gives 8x−20=6x+1268x−20=6x+126, then 2x=1462x=146 and x=73x=73​. Check, 564564 to 188188 is 33 to 11. Writing 5(x−4)5(x−4) as 5x−45x−4 instead gives x=65x=65, where the sides are 500500 and 172172, not a 3:13:1 pair.
Key idea
Cross-multiplying a ratio. From xy=abyx​=ba​ with yy and bb not zero, multiplying both sides by yy and then by bb gives bx=aybx=ay. That is chapter 4's move of multiplying both sides by the same nonzero number, used twice, not a new rule. A numerator with more than one term is multiplied whole, and its parentheses stay. What is left has no fraction and no power, so one such equation in one unknown is chapter 4 work and two in two letters is a chapter 5 system. Every pair x=akx=ak, y=bky=bk satisfies bx=aybx=ay, so the two ways of writing a ratio agree.

An amount can be added to one part, taken from one part, or moved between the two, and the problem states the new ratio. Write the starting amounts as akak and bkbk, adjust each by what moved, and that second statement is one equation in kk. The two ratios have separate multipliers, so 13k13k and 4k4k cannot also be 10k10k and 3k3k.

Problem
A club's juniors and seniors are in the ratio 11:811:8. Then 42 juniors join, no one leaves, and the ratio of juniors to seniors is now 3:23:2. Enter how many juniors the club had before those 42 joined.
Show a hint
  • The senior count never changes, so write both starting counts from the first ratio and adjust only the junior count.
  • With 11k11k juniors and 8k8k seniors, the counts afterwards are 11k+4211k+42 and 8k8k, so the second statement is 11k+428k=328k11k+42​=23​.
Show the full solution
With 11k11k juniors and 8k8k seniors, the ratio after the 42 join is 11k+428k=328k11k+42​=23​. Cross-multiplying gives 22k+84=24k22k+84=24k, so 2k=842k=84 and k=42k=42, and the juniors before were 11(42)=46211(42)=462​. Check, the 336336 seniors are unchanged and 504:336504:336 reduces to 3:23:2, so the 504504 is the count after, not the one asked for. Naming both counts instead gives the system 8j=11s8j=11s and 2j+84=3s2j+84=3s, and elimination reaches the same j=462j=462.
Fun fact
Around 350 BCE Eudoxus of Cnidus built the theory of proportion Euclid kept as Book V of the Elements. It compared ratios of lengths where no unit fits a whole number of times into both, such as a square's side and its diagonal.

The same quantity can appear in two ratios with a different number in each. In x:y=7:6x:y=7:6 the quantity yy is 66 parts, and in y:z=9:2y:z=9:2 it is 99, and those parts are not the same size. Scale each ratio, both parts by the same factor, until the two numbers for yy agree. The three amounts are then in one ratio x:y:zx:y:z.

Problem
In a stockroom, the ratio of blue crates to green crates is 15:815:8, and the ratio of green crates to red crates is 8:118:11. There are 165165 blue crates. Enter the number of red crates.
Show a hint
  • Both ratios use the same number, 88, for the green crates, so blue, green, and red fit into one three-part ratio without rescaling either ratio.
  • Write that three-part ratio, then compare its blue part with the 165165 actual blue crates to get the multiplier that turns parts into counts.
Show the full solution
Both ratios use 88 for green, so blue to green to red is 15:8:1115:8:11. The blue part gives 15k=16515k=165, so k=11k=11, and the red count is 11k=12111k=121​. Green is 8k=888k=88, and the checks pass, 165:88=15:8165:88=15:8 and 88:121=8:1188:121=8:11. The chain is direct only because the shared quantity has the same number in both ratios.
Problem
For three quantities xx, yy, and zz, x:y=16:9x:y=16:9 and y:z=6:13y:z=6:13. Enter zxxz​ as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show a hint
  • In one statement yy is 99 parts and in the other it is 66, and those parts are not the same size. Scale each ratio, multiplying both of its parts by the same factor, until the two numbers for yy match.
  • The least common multiple of 99 and 66 is 1818, so double both parts of 16:916:9 and triple both parts of 6:136:13.
Show the full solution
Doubling 16:916:9 gives 32:1832:18 and tripling 6:136:13 gives 18:3918:39, so with yy at 1818 parts in both, x:y:z=32:18:39x:y:z=32:18:39 and zx=3932xz​=3239​​. Stacking the printed numbers gives 13161613​ instead, which is the trap, since the 99 and the 66 stand for different sizes of part.
Key idea
Matching the shared term. Multiplying every part of a ratio by the same nonzero number leaves the comparison unchanged, so a:ba:b and ac:bcac:bc say the same thing. To combine x:y=a:bx:y=a:b with y:z=c:dy:z=c:d, multiply every part of the first by cc and every part of the second by bb. In both, yy is then bcbc parts, so x:y:z=ac:bc:bdx:y:z=ac:bc:bd and zx=bdacxz​=acbd​, fixed without any amount known. Scaling to any common multiple of bb and cc works, and the least one keeps the numbers small. Scaling only the shared part breaks the statement it came from.

A ratio is one equation in two letters, so neither amount follows from it alone. Adding a second fact about the same two amounts makes a system, and 5.1 counted two equations in two letters as usually enough. It can be a total, a difference, one amount, or the ratio after a change. Cross-multiply the ratio, then use substitution or elimination.

Problem
A caterer orders bread rolls and pastries, rolls to pastries in the ratio 11:611:6. Rolls cost 2 dollars each, pastries cost 5 dollars each, and the order comes to 468 dollars. Enter the number of pastries.
Show a hint
  • The ratio is one fact about the two counts and the total cost is another, so there are two equations in two letters here.
  • With rr rolls and pp pastries, cross-multiplying the ratio gives 6r=11p6r=11p, and the cost gives 2r+5p=4682r+5p=468. Tripling the cost equation makes its rr-term 6r6r, which matches the ratio equation.
Show the full solution
Cross-multiplying the ratio gives 6r=11p6r=11p, and the cost gives 2r+5p=4682r+5p=468. Tripling the cost equation makes it 6r+15p=14046r+15p=1404, so replacing 6r6r with 11p11p leaves 26p=140426p=1404 and p=54p=54​. Then r=99r=99, and 2(99)+5(54)=4682(99)+5(54)=468 checks, though the 9999 is the roll count and not the ask. Writing the counts as 11k11k and 6k6k instead gives 52k=46852k=468 and the same pair.
Problem
A library shelves fiction and nonfiction in the ratio 11:711:7. Then 45 books move from fiction to nonfiction, nothing is added or discarded, and the ratio of fiction to nonfiction reads 4:34:3. Enter how many fiction books the library had before the move.
Show a hint
  • After the move there are 4545 fewer fiction books and 4545 more nonfiction books. Write both starting counts with one letter, using the first ratio.
  • With 11k11k fiction and 7k7k nonfiction, the second ratio gives 3(11k−45)=4(7k+45)3(11k−45)=4(7k+45).
Show the full solution
With 11k11k fiction and 7k7k nonfiction the new ratio gives 11k−457k+45=437k+4511k−45​=34​, so 33k−135=28k+18033k−135=28k+180, then 5k=3155k=315 and k=63k=63. The fiction count before the move was 11(63)=69311(63)=693​. The nonfiction count was 441441, and after the move 648:486648:486 reduces to 4:34:3. The usual slip is adding the 4545 to fiction and taking it off nonfiction, which gives 5k=−3155k=−315 and a negative count, so it rules itself out.
Key idea
Proportion, not size. From a:ba:b alone every proportion among the amounts is known, the share each part is of the whole and the ratio of any two parts, and not one amount is known. Cross-multiplied the statement is bx=aybx=ay, one equation in two letters, which 5.1 already counted as infinitely many pairs, one for each kk. So a question about a share of the whole needs only the ratio, while a question about a count always needs a second fact, independent of the first. Restating the same ratio in bigger numbers is not independent and adds nothing.
Problem
A festival sells full-price, student, and child tickets. Of the tickets sold, full-price to student is 7:47:4, and student to child is 6:116:11. The festival then sells another 75 child tickets, with no change to the other two counts, and full-price to child is now 7:97:9. Enter the number of student tickets sold.
Show a hint
  • In one ratio the student tickets are 44 parts and in the other they are 66, and those parts are not the same size. Combine the two statements into a single three-part ratio before naming any letter.
  • Matching the student number at 1212 makes the three-part ratio 21:12:2221:12:22, so the counts are 21k21k, 12k12k and 22k22k, and the last fact cross-multiplies to 9(21k)=7(22k+75)9(21k)=7(22k+75).
Show the full solution
Matching the student number at 1212 turns 7:47:4 into 21:1221:12 and 6:116:11 into 12:2212:22, so the counts are 21k21k, 12k12k and 22k22k. The last fact gives 21k22k+75=7922k+7521k​=97​, so 189k=154k+525189k=154k+525, then 35k=52535k=525 and k=15k=15. The student count is 12(15)=18012(15)=180​. Check, full-price 315315 against child 405405 is 7:97:9. The letter solved for is kk, so 1515 is a part size and not a ticket count.

Every problem here put one letter on the size of a part or cross-multiplied a ratio into bx=aybx=ay, and no count came without a second fact. Lesson 6.2, Conversion Factors, uses a ratio of another kind, where the two parts are one amount written in two units. The question there is what such a ratio is worth and what multiplying by it does.

Practice these ideas

Practice
A crate holds 340 tiles, each one either plain or patterned. The ratio of plain tiles to patterned tiles is 9:119:11. Enter the number of plain tiles.
Show the solution
9k+11k=3409k+11k=340 gives 20k=34020k=340, so k=17k=17 and the plain tiles number 9(17)=1539(17)=153​. The patterned count is 11(17)=18711(17)=187, and 153+187=340153+187=340.
Practice
A crate holds pears and quinces and nothing else, in the ratio 6:116:11. Enter the fraction of the fruit that is quinces, in lowest terms.
Show the solution
The counts are 6k6k and 11k11k, so the crate holds 17k17k pieces and the quinces are 11k17k17k11k​ of it, which is 11171711​​. A common wrong answer is 116611​, the quince count over the pear count rather than over the whole crate, and a share of the crate cannot be more than 11.
Practice
In a choir, the ratio of altos to sopranos is 8:138:13, and there are 296 altos. Enter the number of sopranos.
Show the solution
The altos are 88 parts, so 8k=2968k=296 and k=37k=37, which makes the sopranos 13(37)=48113(37)=481​. Check, 296:481296:481 reduces to 8:138:13. No total is stated here and none is needed, since one amount fixes kk on its own.
Practice
A jar holds only amber, jade and onyx marbles, in the ratio 9:16:59:16:5. Enter the fraction of the marbles in the jar that are jade, in lowest terms.
Show the solution
The counts are 9k9k, 16k16k and 5k5k, so the jar holds 30k30k marbles and the jade share is 16k30k=81530k16k​=158​​. With three parts the share of the whole is still one part over the sum of all the parts, and 169916​ or 165516​ would each compare jade with one other colour instead.
Practice
A silo holds 494 sacks of wheat, rye and oats in the ratio 5:9:125:9:12. Enter the number of sacks of oats.
Show the solution
Write the counts as 5k5k, 9k9k, and 12k12k. Then 26k=49426k=494, so k=19k=19 and the oat count is 12(19)=22812(19)=228​. The other two are 5(19)=955(19)=95 wheat and 9(19)=1719(19)=171 rye, and 95+171+228=49495+171+228=494.
Practice
A workshop stocks screws, bolts and rivets in the ratio 11:6:411:6:4, and there are 156 bolts. Enter the total number of screws, bolts and rivets.
Show the solution
Each part is kk pieces, and the bolts are 66 parts, so 6k=1566k=156 and k=26k=26. The three counts together are 11+6+4=2111+6+4=21 parts, so the total is 21×26=54621×26=546​. Counting by kind, that is 286286 screws, 156156 bolts and 104104 rivets, and 286+156+104=546286+156+104=546.
Practice
The equation x84=171284x​=1217​ holds. Cross-multiply and enter xx.
Show the solution
Cross-multiplying gives 12x=142812x=1428, so x=119x=119​. Cancelling the 1212 into the 8484 first turns the whole thing into 17×717×7, which is faster than multiplying and then dividing.
Practice
Cross-multiply 7x−122x+50=532x+507x−12​=35​, collect the xx-terms on one side and the numbers on the other, and enter xx.
Show the solution
Cross-multiply, 3(7x−12)=5(2x+50)3(7x−12)=5(2x+50), so 21x−36=10x+25021x−36=10x+250, then 11x=28611x=286 and x=26x=26​. Check, at x=26x=26 the fraction is 170102102170​, which reduces to 5335​.
Practice
Two accounts hold money in the ratio 17:817:8, and the first holds 288 dollars more than the second. Enter the balance of the smaller account, in dollars.
Show the solution
With balances 17k17k and 8k8k, the gap is 17k−8k=9k17k−8k=9k, so 9k=2889k=288 and k=32k=32, and the smaller balance is 8(32)=2568(32)=256​. The other balance is 544544, and 544−256=288544−256=288, with 544:256544:256 equal to 17:817:8 in lowest terms. A difference is enough to find kk, the same as a total would be.
Practice
A stall sells notebooks and folders in the ratio 9:79:7. Notebooks cost 6 dollars each, folders cost 11 dollars each, and the stall takes 1572 dollars for them. Enter the number of folders sold.
Show the solution
With 9k9k notebooks and 7k7k folders, the money gives 54k+77k=157254k+77k=1572, so 131k=1572131k=1572 and k=12k=12, which makes the folder count 7(12)=847(12)=84​. There are 108108 notebooks, and 648+924=1572648+924=1572 checks. The ratio alone fixes neither count, and the takings are the second fact that does.
Practice
Two positive whole numbers are in the ratio 13:613:6, and both are less than 200200. Enter how many such pairs there are.
Show the solution
Every such pair is 13k13k and 6k6k for a positive whole number kk, and 6k6k is the smaller of the two, so the only condition is that 13k13k stays under 200200. Since 13×15=19513×15=195 and 13×16=20813×16=208, kk can be 11 through 1515, a count of 1515​. Without the limit there would be one such pair for every kk, endlessly many.
Practice
In a model kit, pegs and struts come in the ratio 10:310:3, and struts and panels come in the ratio 3:43:4. A batch of these parts has 7676 panels. Enter the number of pegs in the batch.
Show the solution
The struts match at 33 in both ratios, so pegs to struts to panels is 10:3:410:3:4. The panels give 4k=764k=76, so k=19k=19 and the pegs number 10(19)=19010(19)=190​. If the two strut counts had differed, both ratios would need scaling to a common strut count first.
Practice
A field holds 682 plants, all of them corn, beans or squash. Corn to beans is 6:56:5 and beans to squash is 10:910:9. Enter the number of squash plants.
Show the solution
Doubling 6:56:5 gives 12:1012:10, which matches the beans in 10:910:9, so corn to beans to squash is 12:10:912:10:9. The three parts add to 3131, one part is 68231=2231682​=22 plants, and squash is 9(22)=1989(22)=198​. Corn and beans come out to 264264 and 220220, and 264+220+198=682264+220+198=682.
Practice
A survey counts mm walkers, nn cyclists and pp drivers, with mm to nn as 5:125:12 and nn to pp as 8:98:9. Scale so the two numbers for nn agree, then enter pmmp​ as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show the solution
Doubling 5:125:12 gives 10:2410:24 and tripling 8:98:9 gives 24:2724:27, so m:n:p=10:24:27m:n:p=10:24:27 and pm=2710mp​=1027​​. Using the printed numbers straight gives 9559​, which is wrong because nn is 1212 parts in the first ratio and 88 parts in the second.
Practice
A pantry stocks honey jars and jam jars in the ratio 10:710:7. After 48 more honey jars arrive and no new jam jars, the ratio of honey to jam is 8:58:5. Enter the number of jam jars.
Show the solution
Write the counts as 10k10k honey jars and 7k7k jam jars. Then 10k+487k=857k10k+48​=58​, and cross-multiplying gives 50k+240=56k50k+240=56k, so 6k=2406k=240, k=40k=40 and the jam count is 7(40)=2807(40)=280​. Check, the honey counts are 400400 and 448448, and 448:280448:280 reduces to 8:58:5. The 400400 is honey, not the count asked for.
Practice
A vault holds silver and copper coins, and the ratio of silver to copper is 9:49:4. The owner removes 32 silver coins and puts in 32 copper coins, after which the ratio of silver to copper is 5:45:4. Enter the number of silver coins the vault held at the start.
Show the solution
With 9k9k silver and 4k4k copper at the start, the new ratio gives 4(9k−32)=5(4k+32)4(9k−32)=5(4k+32), so 36k−128=20k+16036k−128=20k+160, then 16k=28816k=288 and k=18k=18. The starting silver count is 9(18)=1629(18)=162​. The vault began with 162162 silver and 7272 copper, and afterwards 130:104130:104 reduces to 5:45:4.
Practice
At a gallery, the ratio of prints to paintings is 16:716:7. Then 26 prints are sold and 13 paintings are added, and the ratio of prints to paintings is now 5:35:3. Enter the total number of prints and paintings after the change.
Show the solution
With 16k16k prints and 7k7k paintings, the new ratio gives 3(16k−26)=5(7k+13)3(16k−26)=5(7k+13), so 48k−78=35k+6548k−78=35k+65, then 13k=14313k=143 and k=11k=11. The gallery held 176176 prints and 7777 paintings, and afterwards 150150 and 9090, a total of 240240​. The check is that 150:90150:90 reduces to 5:35:3, and the total fell from 253253 because 26 works left and only 13 came in.
Practice
A cabinet holds oak, ash and birch dowels and nothing else, with oak to ash 9:59:5 and ash to birch 15:815:8. After 105 more birch dowels arrive, the birch count equals the ash count. Enter the total number of dowels the cabinet held before that delivery.
Show the solution
Triple 9:59:5 to get 27:1527:15, so both statements now use 1515 for the ash and oak to ash to birch is 27:15:827:15:8. With the counts 27k27k, 15k15k and 8k8k, equal counts after the delivery mean 8k+105=15k8k+105=15k, so 7k=1057k=105 and k=15k=15. The parts total 5050, so the cabinet held 50(15)=75050(15)=750​. The counts are 405405 oak, 225225 ash and 120120 birch, and 120+105=225120+105=225 as required.
